story.title: Travel Diaries
paragraphs_en: Nina is travelling in the train for the first time!
Nina does not look happy at all! Nina's family is travelling from Kolkata to New Delhi.

"Do we really HAVE to leave Kolkata? My friends and grandparents are going to miss me a lot. Also, where else will I eat Puchka? Daddy, cannot you find a job in Kolkata itself? " Nina asked her father.
"Don't worry, Nina. You will make new friends. You will also find new places to eat Puchka" consoled her father. But, Nina could not be convinced. Her mother and father tried a lot to cheer her up.
They offered her a variety of food items in order to cheer her up. But,Nina was very adamant. 'I don't want to eat anything! ' huffed Nina.
Nina's parents had lost all of the ways to console her. Suddenly, Nina's father smiled. "I can see something there...." he began. "Oh yay! I love this game!" said her mother.
"I can see something in brown colour" her father told them.
"Are they slippers? Or are they mountains? Oh oh, they must be suitcases!" exclaimed her mother.
" You are right- they are suitcases" her father confirmed and clapped his hands. Nina's attention shifted from her book to the game.

" It's my turn now. I can see something in yellow" her mother told them. "You mean, mustard fields? " her father guessed. "It's my hairband!" said Nina. "That's right!" said her mother and clapped hands.
Nina started laughing and participated in the game. "I can see something in blue" started Nina. "The skies!" her mother told them.
"I can see something in brown there.." her mother told them. "The mountains!" guessed her father. "I can see something in white colour.." said her father. "That's a cow!" exclaimed Nina.

"There is something in green color..." started Nina and pat came the reply from her parents that it was grass she was referring to. Her mother spotted something in black and Nina identified it as a crow.

Her father spotted something tall in brown color. It also had spots. "Are you referring to a leopard?" asked her mother. "No! It is a giraffe!" Nina looked outside through the window and said 'Indian forest don't have giraffes. You are pulling our legs!" Everyone started laughing.

Her parents spread a blanket on the seat. They also got the pillow ready for Nina. "Shall we play this game after going to Delhi?" asked Nina. "Ofcourse! The game will be much more fun in a new place!" her father told her.
